subject.title: [Feature]: Add a visible browser panel to the Control UI for login handoff and browser management

question: Should the browser-login handoff surface be built as a core Control UI browser panel now, or should it wait for the generic plugin UI entry-point/contribution-slot direction?
rationale: The missing behavior is real, but the implementation exposes authenticated browser state and overlaps active generic Control UI extension work, so automation should not choose the UX/security boundary alone.

options.title: Core operator handoff panel
options.body: Build a first-party Control UI browser panel with strict operator scopes, redaction, passive status by default, explicit tab/write actions, and same-state resume semantics.

options.title: Gate on plugin UI direction
options.body: Keep this issue open until plugin UI entry points or contribution slots settle, then implement the browser surface through that approved host-owned UI seam.

options.title: Defer visible browser UI
options.body: Keep the current CLI/tool/browser.request primitives and document them as the supported workaround while closing or deprioritizing the panel idea separately.

recommendation.title: Core operator handoff panel
recommendation.body: Build a first-party Control UI browser panel with strict operator scopes, redaction, passive status by default, explicit tab/write actions, and same-state resume semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: He already identified this issue as canonical and has recent history on the Control UI navigation surface.
